critical_steps: Each factor quadratic form equals the negative Hilbert norm square.
The tensor of the two negative second components is positive, giving the exact Parseval tensor identity.
A positive product q1(f)q2(g) forces all q1 values onto one complex ray and all q2 values onto the reciprocal ray.
Reciprocal unimodular rotations preserve the tensor pair and make both factor quadratic forms positive.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact one-point one-dimensional counterexample plus an algebraic phase-classification argument.
integrity.unproved_limits: No separate claim is made that weak measurability alone justifies all factorization steps without an integrability hypothesis.

scientific_limitations: The phase-corrected equivalence assumes the scalar factor integrals exist and the tensor integral factors as their product.
The counterexample itself is finite and does not rely on any Fubini or integrability assumption.
The finding addresses the converse of the tensor-factor theorem and does not assess unrelated results in the source.
A nonindexed correction or informal note may contain the same observation.
title: Tensor positivity determines continuous-biframe factors only up to reciprocal phase
